context_as_of: As of Nov 2026: (1) Facebook Lite launched in June 2015 as an Android app under 1 MB built for 2G networks and low-end phones; current downloads are reported at roughly 2-3 MB (third-party, [uncertain]). (2) Meta last officially disclosed Lite users at 100 mn MAU (Mar 2016, TechCrunch/Business Standard) and 200 mn (Feb 2017, GSMArena); AppGoblin estimates about 400 mn MAU today (third-party estimate, [uncertain]). (3) The app is still updated on Android (Play Store updates May-July 2026 per app-listing sites); the iOS version was withdrawn around 2020 [uncertain]. Messenger Lite was shut down in 2023-24 [uncertain], so Lite now routes messaging into the main Messenger or an in-app inbox. (4) Meta family daily active people were 3.64 bn in Sep 2026 (+3% YoY) and Q3 2026 revenue was $64.6 bn (+26%) (Meta press release, 21 Oct 2026: https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2026/Meta-Reports-Third-Quarter-2026-Results/). Growth is now concentrated in emerging markets where devices and networks are weak, which is Lite's home. (5) India is Facebook's largest country by users; Jio-era cheap data has reduced the 2G problem, but entry-level phones with low storage, data-saver habits and patchy rural coverage remain. Flag: Lite user numbers are stale or third-party; treat them as approximate.
regulatory_context: (1) Net neutrality in India: TRAI's 2016 Prohibition of Discriminatory Tariffs regulation ended Facebook's Free Basics and bars zero-rating deals, so Lite cannot grow through free-data telecom bundles in India - it has to win on efficiency. (2) Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 and DPDP Rules 2025 (India), plus similar laws in Brazil (LGPD), Indonesia (PDP Law) and Nigeria (NDPA): consent, children's data (verifiable parental consent under 18 in India) and data-localisation questions shape what Lite can log for metrics. (3) India IT Rules 2021 (significant social media intermediary duties: grievance officers, traceability debates, takedown timelines) apply to Lite equally. (4) Content and age rules in several markets mean integrity metrics must be market-specific. None of these change the North Star, but they constrain growth tactics and data collection.

framework_applied: Success Metrics framework (frameworks.md section 5). Step 1 Company and product - Meta's mission is connecting people; Facebook Lite exists so that people on weak phones, slow or costly networks can still use Facebook, extending Meta's reach and future ad revenue in emerging markets. Step 2 Users and value - Lite users (first-time internet users, low-storage Android owners, data-budget-conscious users, rural users on patchy networks) go through activation (install and first feed load on a weak network, first friend connection), engagement (sessions, feed views, posts, comments, messages, Groups), conversion (ad views, Marketplace actions) and retention (D30 and weekly return); creators and advertisers are the other sides. Step 3 North Star - Weekly Lite users with a meaningful interaction (MSI: like, comment, share, message or post) completed in a low-cost session; formula = reach (installs) x activation (first successful feed on weak network) x retention (W4 return) x interaction rate; supporting metrics: time to first feed, data MB per session, crash/ANR rate. Step 4 Guardrails - data used per session, app size, battery, cannibalisation of the main app among users who can run it, ad revenue per user, integrity (spam/misinformation) and notification opt-outs.
clarifying_questions: Q: Is Facebook Lite a separate team with its own goal, or just a distribution channel for Facebook? A: Separate team inside the Facebook app org, with its own goal set annually.
Q: Which markets matter most? A: India, Indonesia, Philippines, Nigeria, Bangladesh and Brazil are the biggest; assume India is the largest single market.

Q: Who is the target user - people who can't run the main app, or anyone who prefers a light app? A: Primarily people whose phone, network or data budget makes the main app a poor experience; others are welcome but not the focus.
Q: Is the goal growth in new users, engagement, or monetisation? A: Leadership says connect the next billion and keep them; monetisation matters but is secondary for Lite.
Q: Do we treat a user moving from Lite to the main app as a loss? A: No, if their phone and network allow it, that's a good outcome for Meta.
Q: Any constraints on app size or data use? A: The app must stay under a few MB and work on 2G/3G; the data cost per session is a public promise.
Q: Time frame? A: Goals for the next 12 months.
interviewer_data_reveals: Exhibit 1 (illustrative) - Lite funnel in India, last quarter: Play Store page views 100 -> installs 42 -> first feed loaded within 10 seconds 31 -> added 3+ friends in week 1 19 -> active in week 4 12.
Exhibit 2 (illustrative) - Median time to first feed on Lite: 4G 2.1 s; 3G 5.8 s; 2G/edge 14.5 s. W4 retention: 41% when first feed loads in under 5 s vs 18% when over 15 s.

Exhibit 3 (illustrative) - Data use per 10-minute session: Lite 3.2 MB (text + compressed images); main Facebook app 38 MB (autoplay video). Lite users run out of daily data packs on 22% of days vs 9% for main-app users.
Exhibit 4 (illustrative) - Lite users on phones with 4 GB+ RAM and 4G: 35% of Lite DAU; their ad revenue per user is 45% lower than comparable main-app users.
Exhibit 5 (real, stale) - Meta-reported Lite MAU: 100 mn (Mar 2016), 200 mn (Feb 2017); Meta family DAP 3.64 bn (Sep 2026).

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Set the goals and metrics for Facebook Lite.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: I'll go in four steps: what Facebook Lite is for within Meta, who its users are and how they get value, a North Star with its levers, and guardrails. First a few clarifying questions.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Sure.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Is Lite a separate team with its own goal? Which markets matter most? Is the target user someone who can't run the main app, or anyone? And is it a loss if a Lite user moves to the main app?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Separate team. India, Indonesia, Philippines, Nigeria, Bangladesh, Brazil - India is largest. Target is people whose phone, network or data budget make the main app bad. Moving to the main app is fine. Goals for 12 months.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Company context: Meta has about 3.64 bn daily active people across its apps; growth now comes mostly from emerging markets. Lite's job is inclusion - make Facebook work on a Rs 6,000 phone with 32 GB storage, a shaky network and a 1.5 GB-a-day data pack - so those people join and stay, which protects Meta's reach and its future ad base. In India it can't buy growth with zero-rated data, because TRAI banned that in 2016, so it must win on efficiency.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Goal statement: help people with low-end phones and expensive or weak connectivity build and keep meaningful connections on Facebook, at the lowest data and device cost.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Users: (1) first-time internet users, often in Tier 2-3 towns and villages, comfortable in Hindi or regional languages; (2) users with low storage who uninstall heavy apps; (3) data-budget-conscious users who switch off video; (4) users in areas with patchy coverage. The other sides are friends who interact with them, creators and Pages, and advertisers. Does that cover it?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Yes.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Journey for the Lite user: activation is install plus the first feed loaded on their network and finding a few friends; engagement is opening the app, scrolling, reacting, commenting, messaging and Groups; conversion is seeing ads and using Marketplace; retention is coming back each week. Meta makes money from ads, so impressions matter, but for Lite they come second to keeping users.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Here's the funnel - Exhibit 1. Of 100 store-page views: 42 install, 31 get the first feed in 10 seconds, 19 add 3+ friends in week 1, 12 are active in week 4.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: The largest drop is install to week 4, and two steps stand out: first feed speed (42 to 31) and friend connections (31 to 19). That tells me the North Star should capture a user who is getting real social value, not just opening the app.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: North Star: Weekly Meaningful Lite Users - Lite users who, in a week, complete at least one meaningful social interaction (comment, reply, message, share or post that someone else responds to). Opening the app on a weak network and seeing a spinner is not value; a reply from a cousin is.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text:
Formula:
Weekly Meaningful Lite Users = new installs x activation rate (first feed loaded fast + 3 friends in week 1) x W4 retention x meaningful interaction rate + resurrected users
Supporting metrics: (a) time to first feed by network type; (b) data used per session (MB); (c) crash and ANR rate on 1-2 GB RAM phones; (d) friend connections in week 1; (e) share of content in the user's language.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Exhibit 2: time to first feed is 2.1 s on 4G, 5.8 s on 3G, 14.5 s on 2G. W4 retention is 41% if the first feed loads in under 5 s and 18% over 15 s.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: So performance is a product lever, not just engineering hygiene. I'd make 'percentage of sessions with first feed under 5 seconds on 3G and below' a team goal. I'd want an experiment - for example a text-first feed that loads images later - to show the link is causal and not that 2G users are simply different.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Exhibit 3: Lite uses 3.2 MB per 10-minute session against 38 MB for the main app. Lite users run out of their daily data pack on 22% of days.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: That's the core promise. Data per session is both a supporting metric and a guardrail: features like video previews will raise engagement but can push users over their pack and stop them using the app at all that day. I'd track 'days with a session after data runs out' too - a good sign that offline caching works.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Exhibit 4: 35% of Lite DAU have 4 GB+ RAM phones and 4G, and their ad revenue per user is 45% lower than comparable main-app users.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: That's the cannibalisation risk. Since moving to the main app is fine, I would not count those users as Lite failures. I'd track 'graduation rate' - capable users who move to the main app - and set a guardrail so Lite growth doesn't come from capable main-app users downgrading. Total Meta ad revenue across both apps for the same users must not fall.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: What are your goals for the year then?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Three goals. Goal 1, Reach and keep: grow Weekly Meaningful Lite Users by, say, 15% in India and Southeast Asia. Goal 2, Speed and cost: 80% of sessions on 3G or below show the first feed within 5 seconds, and data per session stays below about 4 MB. Goal 3, Healthy ecosystem: graduation rate up, and no fall in combined ad revenue for users who could use either app.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Guardrails?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Data used per session and app size (must stay a few MB), battery and storage, crash and ANR rates on low-end devices, cannibalisation (main-app downgrades and combined ARPU), integrity - spam, scam and misinformation rates, which are a real risk for first-time users - and notification opt-outs, so we don't pump the North Star with spammy pushes.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: What if the North Star goes up but time spent goes down?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: That's fine for Lite, as long as interactions per user hold. Lite users are data-limited; shorter, cheaper sessions with a reply from a friend are success. I'd only worry if interactions or W4 retention fell.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Wrap up.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Facebook Lite's goal is to make Facebook work for people with weak phones and costly data. North Star: Weekly Meaningful Lite Users. The levers are fast first feed on 2G/3G, week-1 friend connections, low data per session and local-language content. Guardrails: data and app size, crashes, cannibalisation of the main app, integrity and notification fatigue.

answer_and_recommendation: Goal: help people on low-end phones and slow or costly networks build and keep meaningful connections on Facebook, at the lowest data and device cost. Ranked metrics: (1) North Star - Weekly Meaningful Lite Users (users with at least one meaningful social interaction in the week, e.g. a comment, reply, message or post that gets a response). (2) Speed/cost supporting metrics - share of sessions on 3G or below with first feed in under 5 seconds (illustrative W4 retention 41% vs 18%), data MB per session (keep near 3-4 MB vs 38 MB on the main app), crash/ANR on 1-2 GB RAM phones. (3) Activation - share of new users with 3+ friend connections and a feed loaded in week 1. Annual goals: +15% Weekly Meaningful Lite Users in core markets; 80% of low-bandwidth sessions under 5 s first feed; combined Meta ad revenue for 'capable' users not down, with a rising graduation rate to the main app. Risks: video-heavy features raising data cost (mitigate with data guardrail and data-saver defaults), cannibalisation of higher-ARPU main-app users (mitigate by tracking combined ARPU and nudging capable users to the main app), and integrity risk for first-time users (mitigate with spam/scam rate guardrails). Closing line: 'Lite succeeds when a person on a cheap phone and a small data pack gets a reply from someone they care about every week - fast, cheaply, and safely.'
counter_metrics_guardrails: (1) Data used per session (MB) and app download/install size - the product's core promise. (2) Battery drain and storage footprint on low-end devices; crash and ANR rate on 1-2 GB RAM phones. (3) Cannibalisation - share of Lite growth coming from users who downgraded from the main app; combined ad revenue per user across Lite and main app for capable users; graduation rate to the main app. (4) Integrity - spam, scam and misinformation report rates and prevalence, especially among first-time internet users; fake account rate. (5) Notification opt-out and uninstall rates, so engagement is not bought with spammy pushes. (6) Ad load and ad-caused data use - ads must not take a disproportionate share of a user's data. (7) Time spent is deliberately not a goal; watch it only alongside interactions.
follow_up_twists: Twist: 'The Reels team wants to add autoplay short video to Lite to raise time spent - approve?' Response: Only as opt-in or on Wi-Fi/4G with a data cap; I'd A/B test it against data per session, data-pack exhaustion days and W4 retention, not time spent.

Twist: 'Lite MAU is flat but Weekly Meaningful Lite Users is up 10% - good or bad?' Response: Good - users are getting more value; I'd check whether flat MAU comes from healthy graduation to the main app or from fewer new installs.

Twist: 'Jio-style cheap 4G is spreading - should Meta sunset Lite in India?' Response: Not until data shows low-end device share and patchy coverage are small; I'd track the share of Indian users who can't run the main app well and set that as the sunset trigger.
common_pitfalls: Copying main-app metrics (time spent, DAU, ad revenue) without adjusting for Lite's purpose - longer sessions can mean higher data cost and lower retention for Lite users.
Treating users moving to the main Facebook app as churn; it is a good outcome if their device and network allow it.
Ignoring performance (time to first feed, crashes on low-RAM phones) as 'engineering', when it is the main driver of retention on 2G/3G.
Forgetting that India's net neutrality rules (TRAI 2016) rule out zero-rated growth, so growth must come from efficiency and local-language value.
skills_tested: structuring, empathy, quant, business sense, prioritisation, communication
